name: Neodymium-doped lanthanum strontium cuprate
equilibrium_context: Three-dimensional superconductivity strongly suppressed by charge stripe order; no Josephson plasmon in the range investigated

driven_states.emergent_property: After near-infrared excitation with E parallel to c, a clear plasma edge appears in the c-axis THz reflectivity, whose position nearly coincides with the Josephson plasma resonance of equally doped LSCO. The conductivity can, however, be described by a Drude model with a very small scattering rate; the imaginary conductivity shows no 1/omega divergence at any time.
driven_states.source: Nishida et al., Phys. Rev. B 107, 174523 (2023), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.107.174523
driven_states.caveat: Important counterpoint: a plasma edge alone does not establish superconductivity. The authors themselves emphasize the absence of the 1/omega divergence and discuss coherent interlayer Drude transport as an alternative. The entry is to be read as a superconductivity-like signature without evidence of a condensate.
driven_states.measured_quantity: c-axis THz reflectivity, and the complex conductivity derived from it

sources: Nishida et al., Phys. Rev. B 107, 174523 (2023), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.107.174523
gaps: Upper temperature limit estimated from the charge-ordering temperature.
